why: The shell-cap refusal goes back to emitting nothing, which is the state issue #356 opens against: `spawnBullet` returns `false` and a refused shot becomes indistinguishable from an input that never happened -- for the player AND for every consumer of the event stream. It is invisible to everything else by construction. No sim state changes, so `BASELINE_HASH` cannot see it; the shot is still correctly refused, so the cap's own assertions still pass; and nothing renders, plays or vibrates today, so no presentation test can see it either -- the audio and haptics cases for this event are deliberately silent until #356's comparison picks a treatment. That combination is exactly why the emit needs its own pin: every OTHER signal in the tree says the code is fine. Killed by the two cases asserting the event's full payload on a player and on a non-player owner, whose control is the third case -- a DEAD owner is also refused and must emit nothing, which is why `reason` is a discriminator rather than a boolean. Scoped to bullets.test.ts; expectFailures counts that scoped run only. The mutation COMMENTS the push out rather than deleting the line: the harness requires a non-empty `replace`, and a commented line is also the more realistic shape of the regression -- someone silencing a cue during debugging and not restoring it.
killedBy: spawnBullet + ownerShellCount emits fire-blocked for a NON-player owner too, since the cap applies to every owner
spawnBullet + ownerShellCount rejects the player's 6th concurrent shell while 5 are live
